input: Set up an emergency contact card in my wallet

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The amount and type of information to include (contacts only, or also medical info, allergies, blood type, insurance) determines how complex the card needs to be.
Knowing who the emergency contacts are (family, friends, doctor) and how many to list shapes the layout and space requirements.
Whether this is for everyday carry, travel, a child, or a specific medical situation changes what information is most critical to include.
Whether the user wants a handwritten card, a printed card, a pre-made template, or a digital wallet card determines the tools and steps needed.
The physical size constraints of the wallet slot and available materials affect what format and how much content can realistically fit.
The user may want a specific style, language, or emphasis (e.g., medical-focused vs. next-of-kin-focused) that shapes the card's layout and wording.
Understanding what 'done well' means — e.g., a first responder can read it instantly, or a family member can be reached quickly — determines what to prioritise on the card.

gold.taskTitle: Create and place emergency contact card in wallet
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to set up a physical or digital emergency contact card stored in their wallet with relevant personal and contact information.

questions.title: What information besides contacts should the card include?
questions.description: Determine whether to include only emergency contacts or also medical details such as blood type, allergies, medications, and insurance information.

questions.title: How many people should be listed as contacts?
questions.description: Clarify the number of emergency contacts (e.g., one primary, two backups) to plan the space and layout of the card.

questions.title: Is this card for yourself, a child, or someone else?
questions.description: Identify whose emergency card this is, as it affects what information is most relevant and how the card should be worded.

questions.title: Do you want to print it, handwrite it, or use a digital format?
questions.description: Determine the creation method — handwritten, home-printed, professionally printed, or a digital wallet card — to outline the right steps and tools.

questions.title: What size is the card slot the card needs to fit?
questions.description: Find out whether a standard credit-card size works or if the wallet slot requires a custom dimension, which affects design and printing choices.

questions.title: Should the card be readable at a glance or include full detail?
questions.description: Establish whether the priority is an ultra-brief, scannable card for first responders or a more detailed reference card for anyone who finds it.

questions.title: Who is the most likely person to use this card in a crisis?
questions.description: Identify the intended reader — a paramedic, a stranger, a family member — so the card's language, layout, and emphasis can be tailored accordingly.
